subject: NimbleSMC: run particle filter at several parameter values

messages.author: 7d907231b4aca656
messages.subject: NimbleSMC: run particle filter at several parameter values
parts:
Hi all

I see that the nimbleSMC documentation constructs particle filters at some parameter values (possibly initialised from some prior), then the filter is compiled, and then it is run at some specified number of partticles. Now, the latter is the only argument that can be passed to the compiled filter. How to pass, instead, parameter values at which the filter is to be run?
Basically I wold like to re-use the compiled filter at a series of different parameter values, without having to re-compile at each possible run.

Minimal example:

library(nimble)
library(nimbleSMC)  

# define the following state-space model (notice the 'a' and 'b' parameters)
exampleCode <- nimbleCode({
  x0 ~ dnorm(0, sd = 1)
  a ~ dunif(0.5,1.5)
  b ~ dnorm(1, sd=0.5)
  x[1] ~ dnorm(a * x0, sd = 1)
  y[1] ~ dnorm(b*x[1], sd = .7)
  for(t in 2:30){
    x[t] ~ dnorm(a * x[t-1], sd = 1)
    y[t] ~ dnorm(b * x[t], sd = .7)
  }
})

obsdata <- list(y = rnorm(30))
model <- nimbleModel(code = exampleCode, data = obsdata)
my_BootF <- buildBootstrapFilter(model, 'x',  
                                 control = list(saveAll = TRUE, thresh = 1))
Cmodel <- compileNimble(model) 
Cmy_BootF <- compileNimble(my_BootF, project = model) 
# Obtain the estimated loglikelihood using m=1000 particles
logLik <- Cmy_BootF$run(m = 1000)

Ok so, the latter will run the compiled filter with 1000 particles at some parameter values randomly sampled from the prior.
I know that I can also specify some specific parameters in the 'inits' input to nimbleModel, but regardless, once the model is compiled then Cmy_BootF$run(m = 1000) will run only that specific configuration, and I will need to recompile each time I want to provide a different set of parameter values.

Instead I would like to use something like (pardon the incorrect syntax, it's just to give an idea):

loglik <- Cmy_BootF$run(m = 1000, a=0.3, b=0.7)  # run the filter at a=0.3, b=0.7
loglik <- Cmy_BootF$run(m = 1000, a=0.5, b=0.3)  # run the filter at a=0.5, b=0.3

*without having to recompile* whenever I change a and b.

How to do this?

Thanks  a lot!

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: NimbleSMC: run particle filter at several parameter values
parts:
Hi Umberto,

The way to do that would be to modify values in the model.  The model is a stateful object that you can manipulate.  The particle filter is an algorithm that uses the model object.

For example, you can change values in the model by
Cmodel$x0 <- 5
and so on.
The model also provides methods for (log probability) calculations and simulations (drawing random values).  Often it is a good idea to do Cmodel$calculate() after changing its values, so that all calculations are up to date from the new values you have put in the model.  Once you have changed the values in the model, if you re-run the filter, it will be using whatever values are currently in the model.
In case you haven't found your way through our User Manual, you can find it at r-nimble.org, and it has some sections that might be helpful on these aspects of how nimble works.

I hope that helps!
Perry
